title: How can notes and coins make the same amount in different ways?
description: Two ways of paying four hundred and thirty two rupees with notes and coins are written as expressions, split into terms and checked, and a third way is found. Keeko's doubt is that a times part and the next times part are one term.
teaching_notes: One idea: each kind of note or coin makes a times term, and the plus signs separate the terms. Ask the child to find another way to make the same amount.

source: Jia must pay ₹432 using notes and coins. Check 4 × 100 +
video_script.why: The child sees several times terms added together, named as terms, worked out and checked against the amount.
video_script.substitution: Change the amount and the notes and coins and the method stays the same: work out each times term, then add.
video_script.anchor: notes and coins laid out to pay four hundred and thirty two rupees
video_script.wrong_answer: four times one hundred plus one times twenty is one term
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko joins two different notes into one term, but the plus sign between them cuts the expression into two terms.
video_script.payoff_line: Both ways give four hundred and thirty two rupees.

final_answer.value: Both ways give ₹432, and 4 × 100 + 3 × 10 + 2 × 1 is another way
final_answer.spoken: both ways give four hundred and thirty two rupees, and four times one hundred plus three times ten plus two times one is another way

names.Jia: everyday child, not a character of the book

maths_rules: each way has four terms, except the third, which has three
video_script.design: One idea: each kind of note or coin is a times term, and the plus signs cut the expression into terms. The notes and coins stay in the anchor band; the working band writes each way. Keeko's doubt: two times parts are one term.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Jia must pay four hundred and thirty two rupees.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The payment uses notes and coins.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Two ways of paying are written as expressions.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>How can we check that both ways pay the right amount?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 4 notes of 100 as one group, 1 note of 20 as one group, 1 note of 10, 2 coins of 1; each group boxed with a plus sign between the boxes

marks.m1: the notes and coins sort into groups of the same kind

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Notes and coins of one kind make a group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Each group is its own part of the payment.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The plus signs join the parts.

marks.m1: the amount to pay is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the amount to pay is four hundred and thirty two rupees.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first way is four times one hundred, plus one times twenty.
Then it adds one times ten, plus two times one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The second way is eight times fifty, one times ten, four times five, and two times one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the terms of each way; the total of each way; one more way

marks.m1: the three things to find are written under the given lines

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to name the terms, find each total, and then find one more way.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first way has four terms.
They are four times one hundred, one times twenty, one times ten, and two times one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Working out each term gives four hundred, twenty, ten and two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The sum of the four terms is four hundred and thirty two.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the second way also has four terms.
They are eight times fifty, one times ten, four times five, and two times one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Working out each term gives four hundred, ten, twenty and two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The sum of the four terms is again four hundred and thirty two.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, use three tens instead of a twenty and a ten.
It is four times one hundred plus three times ten plus two times one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The terms work out to four hundred, thirty and two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Their sum is again four hundred and thirty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Both ways give ₹432; another way is 4 × 100 + 3 × 10 + 2 × 1
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Both ways give four hundred and thirty two rupees.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Another way is four times one hundred plus three times ten plus two times one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the notes and coins
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 4 × 100 + 1 × 20 is one term; the bubble is struck through; a ring drawn round 4 × 100 and another round 1 × 20, the plus sign between them circled

marks.m3: 4 × 100 and 1 × 20 are ringed as two terms with the plus sign circled

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks four times one hundred plus one times twenty is one term.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But the plus sign cuts it into two terms, since the notes differ.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each kind of note or coin makes its own term.
